title: Congenital Chagas Detection And Treatment Cascade In Endemic And Migrant-Serving Systems
summary: Build a verified, country-comparable way to measure the gap from maternal Trypanosoma cruzi screening through newborn confirmation, treatment, and follow-up without mistaking infection estimates for completed prevention coverage.
why_it_matters: Ministries of health, maternal-newborn program directors, and global-health funders must decide whether to finance antenatal screening and infant follow-up in endemic and migrant-serving systems. Verified cascade evidence would identify where an existing prevention pathway is failing, while preventing donors from counting policies, test availability, or medicine donations as delivered mother-to-child prevention.

success_metrics.target: Every country-level output separates maternal screening, maternal diagnosis, newborn testing, infant treatment, and follow-up denominators.
success_metrics.validation_method: Domain reviewer checks the measure dictionary and each output table against the stated numerator, denominator, time reference, and source grain.

success_metrics.target: Every burden, pathway, or coverage claim links to a dated evidence record with method and limitations.
success_metrics.validation_method: Run pnpm validate and spot-check each claim-to-source mapping in evidence.json and evidence.md.

success_metrics.target: At least one replicated country or cross-country analysis identifies a measurable cascade bottleneck without issuing clinical instructions.
success_metrics.validation_method: Replicator reruns the analysis from the documented inputs and confirms the result is suitable for funding or program-design review only.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, infectious-disease domain review, red-team review of screening and treatment misinterpretation, field-reality review for maternal-newborn workflows, and independent replication for quantitative outputs.
